summary: The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited for “ _6. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions and prayer for the grant of an interim tariff. The rival contentions will be considered only at the time of the final tariff order. Therefore, the same are not deliberated in the instant interim order._ _8. As we are not deliberating in detail in this interim order, the prayer for the grant of COD under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations shall be considered in the final order.”_ _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations and is adequate for carrying out prudence check of the claims made, the Commission may consider granting interim tariff in case of new projects._ _(6) The Commission may hear the petitioner, the respondents and any other person permitted including the consumers or consumer associations while granting interim or final tariff.”_ i. The Petitioner has failed to coordinate effectively in statutory meetings regarding the alignment of commissioning schedules for its assets and NHPC's assets. The minutes of the 19th JCC Meeting dated 22. 9.2023 indicate a lack of coordination between the parties. The Petitioner is responsible for the initial commissioning, and proper coordination was expected. - (b) The operationalisation is validated by the CTUIL, the designated statutory authority, and 10. In response, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 8.7.2025 and 22.9.2025 has made the following submissions: a. NHPC's claim of no coordination is incorrect. NHPC responded to both the notices issued by the Petitioner under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, participated in the meetings with regard to the trial operation and was made aware of the provisions of the Tariff Regulations as well as the IEGC with regard to the mismatch. NHPC’s objections are untenable, as the facts with regard to the charging and trial operation of both Assets 2 and 3 speak for themselves. NHPC was kept informed at all stages. Therefore, the allegation that there was lack of coordination on the part of the Petitioner is not correct. 22. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 8.7.2025 has submitted the following clarifications with regard to the issues raised by NHPC: the Petitioner, is solely for the use of NHPC and has not been constructed by it for any other purpose/ use. NHPC's claim of _force majeure_ cannot be addressed in the instant petition. If NHPC seeks to invoke _force majeure_ , it must do so independently in appropriate proceedings. Such a claim cannot be relied upon as a defence to deny or defer the Petitioner’s claim in the present petition. As per Regulation 27(C)(i) of 2023 IEGC Regulations and Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, if regular service is delayed due to commissioning issues not attributable to the licensee, an appropriate petition should be filed before the Commission for its approval. The only issue to be adjudicated by the Commission is whether the Petitioner is entitled to claim deemed COD, having furnished all the necessary documents. The contentions raised by NHPC in its reply are to disentitle the Petitioner from claiming the same. 25. We have considered the submission of the Petitioner and NHPC. We proceed to analyse the contentions of NHPC and the clarifications given by the Petitioner regarding the liability of transmission charges in respect of Asset-2 and Asset-3 in the subsequent paragraphs. The NHPC has submitted that its Project was delayed due to _force majeure_ events, such as unpredictable weather and heavy rainfall, and therefore, NHPC cannot be held liable for transmission charges for such delays. The Petitioner has submitted that the NHPC's claim of _force majeure_ cannot be addressed in the instant petition. If NHPC seeks to invoke _force majeure_ , it must pursue it independently in appropriate proceedings. Such a claim cannot be relied upon as a defence to deny or defer the Petitioner’s claim in the present petition. We have considered the submission of the Petitioner and the Respondent(s). 34. We agree with the contention of the Petitioner that the instant petition is filed for the determination of tariff in respect of its own transmission assets. Any delay on account of force _majeure_ events encountered by the NHPC in commissioning of the Lower Subansiri project cannot be adjudicated in the present petition filed by the Petitioner and may be examined in proceedings to be initiated by NHPC separately. Therefore, we are of the view that the contentions of NHPC regarding delays in commissioning due to force majeure events lack merit and are hereby rejected.
